title: Mecpow Add-Ons: IR Module, Rotary Chuck, Lens Set, Enclosure
metaDescription: Five Mecpow laser add-ons compared: the R1 1064 nm IR module, G5 rotary chuck, X4 Pro lens set, G1 slide extension and FC3 fireproof enclosure, with compatibility notes and prices from $33.10.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: Mecpow sells as many accessories as machines, and the accessory names are cryptic: R1, G5, G1, FC3. This guide decodes five of them: an infrared laser module, a rotary chuck, a replacement lens set, a slide extension and a fireproof enclosure. Prices run from $33.10 to $208.59. The key rule for all of them is compatibility, because each one lists the specific machines it fits and most will not work on anything else.

items.label: R1 1064 nm 1.2W IR Laser Module ($208.59)
items.value: Infrared module for the Mecpow X3, M1, X4 and X5 series and the Creality Falcon A1

items.label: G5 Rotary Chuck with Jaws ($88.28)
items.value: A chuck with jaws for holding round objects for rotary engraving

items.label: X4 Pro 40W / B40W Laser Lens Set, 4 pcs ($33.10)
items.value: Four replacement lenses for the X4 Pro 40W and B40W

items.label: G1 Slide Extension for X1, 370x105 mm ($76.15)
items.value: Extension for the Mecpow X1 engraver

items.label: FC3 Fireproof Enclosure, 1300x730x460 mm ($88.28)
items.value: A fireproof enclosure for the machine and workpiece

pros: The R1 module works across several Mecpow series and the Creality Falcon A1, a rare cross-brand fit
The R1 is also sold in a bundle with the X3S 12W at $441.44, which suits a buyer who plans to use it from day one
The lens set costs only $33.10 for four pieces, a cheap way to keep a 40W machine running
The G1 slide extension is listed at $76.15, a large discount against its $199.99 reference price
The FC3 enclosure at $88.28 is a low-cost fire-safety item
cons: The R1 costs $208.59, more than some complete diode engravers, so it only makes sense if you need what an IR laser does
The G5 chuck listing gives no size range or compatibility, so check the product page before ordering
The lens set fits only the X4 Pro 40W and B40W, and the slide extension only the X1
The FC3 listing gives dimensions but does not say how smoke is vented, so an enclosure does not replace an extractor
The 'was' prices are the seller's reference figures, not proof of a real discount

items.question: What does a 1064 nm IR module do?
items.answer: In general, a 1064 nm infrared laser is used to mark materials such as metals that blue diode lasers do not mark well. Check the listing and the machine's manual for the materials this module supports before buying.

items.question: Can the R1 module be used on any laser?
items.answer: No. The listing names the Mecpow X3, M1, X4 and X5 series and the Creality Falcon A1. Other machines are not stated as compatible.

items.question: Do I need a rotary chuck or a roller?
items.answer: A chuck holds items such as rings or small cylinders, while a roller supports larger round objects such as tumblers. Choose by the shape of what you want to engrave, and check compatibility with your machine.

items.question: How often do lenses need replacing?
items.answer: A lens needs replacing when it is scratched, burnt or coated with residue. A four-piece set is a cheap spare for a 40W machine. Clean lenses carefully according to the manual.

items.question: Does an enclosure make laser work safe?
items.answer: It helps with fire containment, but it does not replace eye protection, ventilation or supervision. Our laser safety guide, "Laser Safety: Fire, Fumes and Eye Protection", covers the basics.

sections.content: Buy add-ons for a specific job, not for completeness. The lens set is a cheap spare if you own the matching machine, the FC3 is a sensible fire-safety purchase, and the R1 module is worth it only if you need to mark metals. Always match the model name in the title to your machine before you pay.
